heroText: London is a vast but readable capital when you plan around the Tube, river and neighbourhoods. Start with Westminster and the Houses of Parliament, cross to the South Bank, then save time for the British Museum or Tower of London. Heathrow is the main long-haul airport, while Gatwick, Stansted, Luton and City shape route choices.

areas.name: Westminster
areas.text: Westminster is best for first-time landmark walks, Parliament views, royal parks and easy Underground access.

areas.name: Covent Garden
areas.text: Covent Garden puts theatres, restaurants, shops and Soho within easy walking distance, but hotels cost more.

areas.name: South Bank
areas.text: South Bank gives river views, cultural venues and walkable routes between Waterloo, Tate Modern and Westminster.

areas.name: Kensington
areas.text: Kensington works for museums, Hyde Park, polished hotels and easier access toward Heathrow routes.

areas.name: Shoreditch
areas.text: Shoreditch suits restaurants, bars, street art and repeat visitors who want East London energy.

airports.name: London Heathrow Airport (LHR)
airports.text: Heathrow is London's main long-haul airport, with Elizabeth line, Tube and rail connections into central districts.

airports.name: London Gatwick Airport (LGW)
airports.text: Gatwick is south of London and works well for rail links to Victoria, London Bridge and Thameslink stations.

airports.name: London City Airport (LCY)
airports.text: London City Airport is closest to Canary Wharf and the City, useful for business trips and short European routes.

airportTransfer.value: 15-60 min depending on airport and rail route
airportTransfer.note: Heathrow has Elizabeth line and Tube links
airportTransfer.distance: about 24 km west of central London from Heathrow

stayOverview: Choose Westminster for landmarks, Covent Garden for theatre and restaurants, South Bank for river culture, Kensington for museums and Heathrow convenience, or Shoreditch for nightlife and a more local East London base.
hotelIntro: London hotel choice is about transport as much as neighbourhood feel. Stay near a useful Tube or Elizabeth line station, then choose between landmark-heavy Westminster, theatre-led Covent Garden, museum-focused Kensington or food-led Shoreditch.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for London; congestion, parking and public transport make it unnecessary until leaving the city.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Pick a hotel near a Tube or Elizabeth line station rather than chasing the absolute geographic centre.

travelTips.title: Airport choice
travelTips.text: Check the airport before booking flights, because Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted, Luton and City have very different transfer routes.

travelTips.title: Payments
travelTips.text: Use contactless cards or mobile wallets on Tube, buses and many rail services instead of buying paper tickets.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Windsor, Oxford and Hampton Court are straightforward rail day trips when you want a break from central London.

history.text: By about 680 the city had become a major port again, but there is little evidence of large-scale production.

history.label: 12th century
history.text: In the 12th century the institutions of central government, which had followed the royal English court around the country, grew in size and sophistication and became increasingly fixed, for most purposes at Westminster, although.
In 1264, during the Second Barons' War, Simon de Montfort's rebels killed 500 Jews while attempting to seize records of debts. Early modern The Reformation produced a shift to Protestantism.
The fortifications failed their only test when the New Model Army entered London in 1647.
The ban was lifted during the 1660 Restoration; London's oldest theatre, Drury Lane, opened in 1663.
In 1666, the Great Fire destroyed much of the wooden-built city.

history.label: 18th century
history.text: During the 18th century London was dogged by crime, and the Bow Street Runners were established in 1750 as a professional police force.
In 1710, Christopher Wren's masterpiece St Paul's Cathedral was completed, replacing its medieval predecessor, lost in the Great Fire.
Following an 1838 fire, the Royal Exchange was rebuilt in 1844.
Lyons opened the first of their chain of teashops in Piccadilly in 1894.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Westminster Abbey, rebuilt in Romanesque style by King Edward the Confessor, was one of the grandest churches in Europe.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Winchester had been the capital of Anglo-Saxon England, but from this time, London became the main forum for foreign traders and the base for defence in time of war.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: It became the basis of a new Palace of Westminster.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: London became the main North Sea port, with migrants from England and abroad.
